subject: [PATCH 03/22] mm: introduce the common-memory node state

2026-11-14.patch_summary: This patch introduces the concept of 'common memory' in Linux, which refers to memory that can be managed by the kernel's MM services without needing explicit node requests. It adds a new node state called N_MEMORY_COMMON and exposes this information through sysfs attributes. The patch also updates documentation and APIs to reflect these changes, allowing userspace to identify nodes with common memory available for ordinary allocations.

reviews.author: Richard Cheng
reviews.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that the patch description does not clearly distinguish between common memory (N_MEMORY_COMMON) and private memory, requesting a clearer distinction to be made.
reviews.raw_body:
This sentense kind of blurred me, you state that N_MEMORY_COMMON is meant
to isolate the concept of #2 from N_MEMORY, I expect something
making clear distinction between common memory and private memory ?

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that N_MEMORY and N_MEMORY_COMMON are initially equivalent, but plans to introduce a new state (N_MEMORY_PRIVATE) in v6 of the patch series, which will make the sets disjoint.
reviews.raw_body:
Sorry, basically as of this set:
  node_state[N_MEMORY] == node_state[N_MEMORY_COMMON]

Later, we'll introduce N_MEMORY_PRIVATE and the sets become disjoint.

I realize posting this series in isolation was a mistake now, and I am
going to post the entire v6 of private nodes with the reworks you
suggested instead.

-- 
~Gregory
